instantiated_cells.justification: The law prohibits engaging in lobbying "as a lobbyist" unless licensed (§13.66), and defines a "lobbyist" as an individual paid by a principal whose duties include lobbying (§13.62(11)), with licensing obtained by application and fee (§13.63(1)(a)).
A lobbyist license (obtained by application) expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, requiring renewal every 24 months.
Lobbyists must file a license application (§13.63) and principals must separately file a registration statement when threshold is met (§13.64), making them independent registrants.
The lobbyist license application must include items like a social security number (or oath of no SSN) and signature, but the statute does not require submission of a photograph.
Elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees are not subject to specified lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity.

An agency that files a statement under §13.695 and named officials are not subject to multiple lobbying provisions (including licensing/registration/reporting sections) except as provided in §13.695, creating a partial exemption for government agencies.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled statutes set deadlines for principals to report changes (§13.695(2) for agencies; §13.64(3) for principals adding new areas) but do not state any deadline for lobbyists to notify the board of changes to their own license/registration information.

The text requires a lobbyist to be licensed and authorized before lobbying (§13.66) but does not specify a numeric 'days after first lobbying' deadline for lobbyist registration; it is a precondition rather than a day-count.
